summary_en: This Phase 2 study compares a fasting mimicking diet with a usual diet in men with metastatic castrate sensitive prostate adenocarcinoma. Participants eat the fasting mimicking diet for 5 days each month for 6 monthly cycles, and all participants receive standard prostate cancer treatment. The study aims to examine effects on response to cancer treatment and metabolic outcomes, and the main outcome measure is not stated.
summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 compara una dieta que imita el ayuno con una dieta habitual en hombres con adenocarcinoma de próstata metastásico sensible a la castración. Los participantes consumen la dieta que imita el ayuno durante 5 días cada mes, en 6 ciclos mensuales, y todos reciben el tratamiento estándar para el cáncer de próstata. El estudio busca examinar los efectos en la respuesta al tratamiento del cáncer y en los resultados metabólicos, y la medida principal de resultado no está indicada en el registro.
who_for: Prostate adenocarcinoma that is metastatic and castrate sensitive, confirmed by biopsy, with metastatic disease confirmed by biopsy or MRI.
Starting or receiving first-line intensified hormone therapy with abiraterone, apalutamide, enzalutamide, or darolutamide, with or without chemotherapy.
Reads, writes, and understands English or Spanish, and has telephone access for contact with the study dietitian.
Able to give written informed consent and comply with study requirements.
not_for: Allergy to any ingredient on the Xentigen ingredient list.
Diabetes without stable diabetes medicine for 6 months, and without physician consent to hold it during fasting days.
Significant heart, lung, or liver disease, or ongoing alcohol or drug abuse, per the study physician.
BMI under 20, actively trying to lose weight, on weight loss medicine, or planning weight loss surgery in the next 6 months.
Self-reported weight loss of 10% or more in the last 6 months.
